subject: Telemetry consolidation + route ownership handoff
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Telemetry consolidation + route ownership handoff

Team —

I'm opening this thread to align on a short plan to consolidate route-level telemetry (cost, p95/p99 latency, failure surface) into a single console surface and to hand off ownership for route correctness and cost investigations. The ask is coming from product — they want a narrow, actionable dashboard we can ship as an alpha for a small set of high-volume routes by end of Q2 (2 weeks).

Key goals:
- Expose per-route token cost (avg + tail) and per-request latency percentiles in one view
- Link traces/errors from the same route slice to easy drilldowns
- Make ownership explicit (who gets alerted on cost spikes or SLA breaches)

Constraints I know about:
- Infra can't add new high-cardinality labels without some ingest cost (Grace, please confirm limit)
- We need a temporary fallback that doesn't require full trace replay to debug cost spikes

I've attached a rough mapping of routes we think matter (route-mapping-v1.csv) and a sample chart for the cost slice (sample-cost-slice.png). Please reply with: 1) feasibility and hard blockers, 2) a brief proposal for how to implement a lightweight alpha (sampling, derived metrics, or existing metrics reshaping), and 3) who will own alerts + follow-up.

If we can agree on an alpha scope today I'll schedule a 30-min sync for tomorrow to finalize owners.

Thanks —
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Product Insights
Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-30T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Telemetry consolidation + route ownership handoff

Thanks Marcus — good framing. A few clarifying questions before we scope the alpha: 

1) Alpha route set: do we constrain to 5 named routes (high-throughput customer-facing) or by traffic percentile (top 10%)? I prefer named routes so we can validate correctness.
2) Metrics backlog: do we want derived per-request token-cost (requires correlating tokens emitted with billing reports) or a proxy (tokens_recorded * cost_per_token_estimate)? The former is ideal but could hit the billing pipeline.
3) Alerts: are we aiming for automated on-call paging or Slack-first notifications for alpha? Slack-first reduces blast radius.

On feasibility, product + data infra can support a sampled derived metric approach for an alpha: we compute sampled per-request token_count and estimate cost, expose p50/p95/p99, and provide links to spans for tail latencies. Sampling would reduce ingest by ~80% vs full replication. Grace — can infra support a sampling flag at the route tag level this week?

Proposed owners for alpha:
- Observability pipeline: lauren_bishop (design + dashboards)
- Runtime / infra contact: grace_oconnor (sampling + label budget)
- Product escalation / stakeholder: evelyn_hart (customer comms + prioritization)

If everyone agrees I'll put a draft scope doc in the Drive and we can lock owners in the sync.

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Sr. Manager, Observability
Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-30T13:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Telemetry consolidation + route ownership handoff

Looping in a quick infra reality check:

- We can enable a sampling flag per route; implementation cost is small and we can have a rollout by EOD tomorrow. Sampling rate configurable.
- Adding a new high-cardinality label to every request is the expensive part (ingest + storage). For alpha: use derived tags that group routes into buckets (route_group) to keep cardinality low.
- We can expose links from the per-route view to existing trace IDs; full trace replay will be in a follow-up.

Attachment: route-mapping-v1.csv — I annotated which routes are safe to sample and which ones are sensitive (PII paths).

Operational ask: we should avoid paging for alpha. Slack-first alerting into #route-cost-alerts and a daily digest is safer while we tune thresholds. If we see deterministic regressions we'll flip to on-call.

I'll own the rollout (infra-side) with a small bite-sized runbook: enable sampling -> validate metrics for 48h -> flip to dashboard. ETA: sampling flag + dashboards wired for the 5-route alpha by 48 hours.

— Grace
Grace O'Connor
Lead, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference
[attachment: route-mapping-v1.csv (text/csv)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-30T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Telemetry consolidation + route ownership handoff

All — thanks for the quick responses and willingness to move fast. Agreed on the named-5-route alpha and Slack-first alerts. Action items: 

- Lauren: draft the alpha dashboard (mock + metric definitions) and drop in Drive by 11:00 PT tomorrow. Add a small explainer on the sampling-estimate trade-off. (owner)
- Grace: enable sampling flag for the five routes and validate metrics for 48 hours. Share the runbook in the Drive. (owner)
- Evelyn: coordinate a short stakeholder note (PMs + Sales) and be the comms owner for initial customers impacted by alerting. (owner)

I'll schedule the 30-min sync for 2028-05-31T09:30:00-07:00 and include a short agenda: scope, owners, rollback criteria.

Thanks — let's treat this as a high-priority alpha; if anyone hits a blocker ping me directly.

Marcus
